label: DISTANCE

cover.headline: When you want *different amounts* of closeness
cover.sub: 5 ways to meet in the middle.

points.heading: It’s common, not a sign of failure
points.body: Two people rarely want exactly the same amount of time together or apart.
points.panel: Name the difference without deciding who is right.

points.heading: Talk about what closeness means
points.body: For one of you it might be talking. For the other, being in the same room.
points.panel: “When do you feel closest to me?”

points.heading: Make space feel safe
points.body: Time apart is easier when it’s clear it isn’t pulling away.
points.panel: “Go enjoy your evening. I’ll be here when you’re back.”

points.heading: Agree on reliable together time
points.body: Knowing closeness is coming makes the space easier for both of you.
points.panel: “Can Sunday mornings be ours, no matter what?”

points.heading: Keep checking in
points.body: Needs shift over the years. What worked last year may need a tweak.

close.save: Save this for the next talk about it.

caption:
One of you wants more time together. The other needs more space. It can feel personal, like one of you cares less.

Usually it isn’t. People simply recharge differently. These five steps help you find a rhythm that works for both of you.

Save this, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
